title: precision electronics joints and serviceable repairs

specimens.name: Precision folded chassis corner with captive threaded inserts
specimens.description: TOP ROW CELL 1 ONLY. Local precision-formed steel chassis corner with one clean 90-degree bend, a short return flange and exactly two captive self-clinching threaded inserts integrated into the metal; no separate loose nuts, bolts, electronics or complete enclosure.

specimens.name: Flush countersunk aluminium lap joint
specimens.description: TOP ROW CELL 2 ONLY. Two short anodized-aluminium panel fragments overlapping in one precise lap joint with an even row of flush countersunk machine-screw heads; joint fragment only, no separate fasteners, frame or enclosure.

specimens.name: Reinforced captive-thread mounting point
specimens.description: TOP ROW CELL 3 ONLY. Small precision sheet-metal fragment with one locally formed reinforcement emboss and one captive threaded insert or rivet-nut for repeated assembly; no loose bolt, bracket, cable, connector or larger panel system.

specimens.name: Precision interlocking tab-and-slot chassis seam
specimens.description: TOP ROW CELL 4 ONLY. Two short CNC-punched/folded sheet-metal fragments joined by a repeatable tab-and-slot seam with clean alignment and minimal local retention; no complete box, rack or cabinet.

specimens.name: Removable rack-ear-to-chassis joint
specimens.description: BOTTOM ROW CELL 1 ONLY. Local anodized-aluminium rack-ear fragment joined to a short electronics-chassis edge through two precise slotted mounting holes and captive service hardware; only the joint, not a full rack ear pair, rail assembly, enclosure or cabinet.

specimens.name: Precision locating dowel-and-bushing service joint
specimens.description: BOTTOM ROW CELL 2 ONLY. Two short precision electronics service-mount plates registered by exactly two hardened tapered locating dowels engaged in matching reamed bushing seats; one visible separable local repeat-alignment joint, no quarter-turn fasteners, threaded inserts, gasket, hatch, whole fixture or cabinet. This is a locating joint, not an access-panel closure.

specimens.name: Replaceable precision reinforcement doubler
specimens.description: BOTTOM ROW CELL 3 ONLY. Small rectangular aluminium/steel reinforcement doubler with two locator features and an even captive-fastener pattern designed for repeatable replacement; no crude weld patch, no mismatched hardware and no surrounding structure.

specimens.name: Rack-rail structural corner node with captive nut strip
specimens.description: BOTTOM ROW CELL 4 ONLY. One local node joining a short rack-specific perforated rail fragment to one short transverse chassis member through a compact precision corner block and captive nut strip; node only, not a complete rack, frame or cabinet.

global_forbidden: text, letters, numbers, logos or pseudo-writing
whole racks, electronic cabinets, complete chassis enclosures, machines, vehicles, buildings, rooms or staged scenes
any ninth or extra specimen, duplicate specimen, omitted specimen, merged specimen or substitution
bolts, screws, nuts, washers or rivets as standalone specimens; embedded fastener heads/hardware are allowed only as part of the listed joints
generic rough welded T-joints, generic bolted lap joints with protruding ordinary nuts, crude field patches, mismatched fasteners or random hole patterns
cables, connectors, electronic modules, motors, controls, displays, lamps or complete service doors/hatches
rust, orange oxidation, heavy chipping, distressed patina or rough hand-cut scars
baked cast shadows, contact shadows, glow, bloom, rays or temporary FX
photorealistic PBR catalog rendering, filtered 3D-render appearance or soft studio-product photography
quarter-turn fasteners or gasketed service-panel edge as the primary specimen 06 mechanism

era_contract.character: late-1990s test-electronics construction using precision formed sheet metal, captive service hardware, rack-specific joints and repeatable disassembly rather than ordinary workshop fastening
required_signals: replaceable locator-based reinforcement and local service joints
repeatable dowel/bushing positional registration rather than another captive panel latch
replaced_previous_language: ordinary protruding bolt-and-nut industrial joints as the dominant language
simple stamped brackets and generic channel/box-section splice nodes
replaceable reinforcement plates relying only on standard loose bolts
forbidden_regressions: generic E1-only bracket/splice language without captive or rack-specific service construction
quarter-turn fasteners or gasketed service-panel edge as the primary specimen 06 mechanism
